sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare – Principles of Chemical Science
sources.source_location: Course Description and unit sequence on atoms, chemical bonding and structure, thermodynamics and chemical equilibrium, transition metals/redox, chemical kinetics and catalysis.

sources.label: IUPAC – Periodic Table of Elements
sources.publisher: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
sources.source_location: Current IUPAC periodic-table page, including standard atomic-weight framing and the distinction between atomic-number organization and recommended atomic-weight values.

sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare – Thermodynamics & Kinetics
sources.source_location: Course Description and syllabus covering macroscopic thermodynamics, reaction and phase equilibrium, and rates of chemical reactions.

sources.label: IUPAC Gold Book – chemical equilibrium
sources.publisher: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
sources.source_location: Current Gold Book definition linking equilibrium to equal forward/reverse rates, Gibbs-energy minimum and the equilibrium constant.

sources.label: IUPAC Gold Book – activation energy
sources.publisher: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
sources.source_location: Current Gold Book definition of activation energy as an empirical parameter characterizing the temperature dependence of the rate coefficient.

sources.label: NIST–JANAF Thermochemical Tables, SRD 13
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.source_location: NIST SRD 13 search interface for thermochemical tables and Gibbs-energy/enthalpy data across chemical species and phases.

sources.label: NIST Chemical Kinetics Database, SRD 17
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.source_location: Current SRD 17 reaction-database interface and welcome documentation for gas-phase kinetics records, rate parameters and bibliographic provenance.

sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare – Laboratory Chemistry
sources.source_location: Course resources and lecture sequence including laboratory measurement/error analysis, X-ray diffraction, mass spectrometry and NMR, plus laboratory notebooks and reports.

sources.label: NIST Chemistry WebBook, SRD 69
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.source_location: NIST SRD 69 overview of thermochemical and thermophysical data plus IR, mass, UV/Vis, vibrational and electronic spectra and chromatography data.

sources.label: IUPAC Gold Book – detection limit
sources.publisher: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
sources.source_location: Current Gold Book definition of detection limit as the minimum result distinguishable from a suitable blank with a stated probability.

sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare – Introduction to Solid-State Chemistry
sources.source_location: Course Description and syllabus linking electronic structure, bonding and atomic order to solid-state materials, including crystallography, semiconductors, defects, glasses, kinetics, polymers and electrochemistry.

sources.label: NIST – Surface Data / X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Database SRD 20
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.source_location: NIST surface-data overview of SRD 20, including reference binding energies, Auger energies, chemical shifts, specimen information and searchable spectral records for surface/material analysis.

sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare – Organic Chemistry I
sources.source_location: Structure and reactivity of organic molecules; substitution, elimination, carbonyl and aromatic chemistry.

sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare – Biological Chemistry I
sources.source_location: Proteins, catalysis, cofactors, metabolism, bioenergetics and macromolecule chemistry.

sources.label: IUPAC – Blue Book: Nomenclature of Organic Chemistry
sources.publisher: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
sources.source_location: Authoritative organic nomenclature and preferred-name framework; online version 3 released December 2023.

sources.label: American Chemical Society – Chemical laboratory safety guidance
sources.source_location: Laboratory safety culture, hazard recognition, risk management and safer instructional chemistry practice.

sources.label: IUPAC – Red Book: Nomenclature of Inorganic Chemistry
sources.publisher: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
sources.source_location: Authoritative nomenclature of inorganic compounds, formulae and coordination/inorganic naming systems.

sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare – Physical Chemistry
sources.source_location: Quantum mechanics for chemists, molecular orbital theory, molecular structure, spectroscopy and photochemistry.

sources.label: MIT OpenCourseWare – Principles of Inorganic Chemistry III
sources.source_location: Main-group inorganic chemistry with synthesis, structure, bonding and reaction mechanisms.
